extracted.intended_audience: aspiring short-story writers and creative-writing students
extracted.subtask_description: Crafting and revising short fiction with attention to compression, form, voice, openings/endings, and iterative revision, as taught in a Joyce Carol Oates MasterClass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read with purpose / careful reading
rubrics_metrics.description: You can't be a writer unless you're reading all the time and reading with purpose — not just reading to waste time, but reading crafted work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze craft choices in the work you read; study very brief narratives (e.g., Williams' 'The Use of Force') to learn what compression demands; reread to understand technique rather than only for pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression / every word must work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short fiction's compression makes weakness immediately visible; because of the form's brevity, each word must earn its place. Study very brief narratives to see how excess is eliminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single sustained effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Single effect (Poe's principle) — a story should produce one sustained emotional or intellectual experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a unified impact rather than competing aims; evaluate whether the piece sustains a coherent emotional/intellectual throughline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensity per word
rubrics_metrics.description: Intensity — short fiction operates at higher pressure per word than novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the story achieves necessary intensity in each paragraph/sentence; note that sagging paragraphs that a novel could survive will harm a short story's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural choice and experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: "It's exciting to experiment with structure"; many stories are best told in elliptical or unusual ways; the conventional shape (rising action, climax, resolution) is one option among many.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose form deliberately: ask whether the form/structure is chosen for this story specifically. Be open to elliptical or unconventional shapes when they serve the story, rather than defaulting to conventional plotting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening — does it open into the story?
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening (does it open into the story?) — openings should enter the story rather than merely set or stall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use close reading (e.g., Hemingway's 'Indian Camp' workshop) to test whether the opening propels the reader into the narrative. An effective opening should immediately engage and begin the story's single effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ending — must land and open outward
rubrics_metrics.description: The short story ending must land — a single sentence often determines the whole; resist tidy resolution; the best endings open outward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the ending delivers the story's emotional/intellectual payoff without closing everything neatly; prefer endings that extend implications beyond the story rather than neatly resolving them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision as substantive reworking
rubrics_metrics.description: Revision is where the real work happens — multiple drafts, not minor edits; the first draft is the discovery; later drafts are the building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect several full rewritings. Look for evidence that the piece has been reshaped over multiple drafts rather than only lightly polished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice — emerges from practice and distinctiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice emerges from persistent practice, not from imitation; your voice is what is left when you stop trying to sound like someone else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the narrator/authorial presence feels distinctive and consistent across the piece and whether it seems the product of an authentic practice rather than mimicry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and transformation of personal experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Write from your own experience but transform it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate material from life, notes, overheard speech and prompts, but reshape and fictionalize experience so it serves the story's single effect rather than functioning as a memoiristic record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating material and habits (notebooks, prompts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use prompts and exercises; maintain notebooks for fragments and overheard speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate a practice of collecting fragments, dialogue, and prompts to supply raw material for stories; use course workbook exercises or prompts to spark scenes and images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of iterative polishing
rubrics_metrics.description: The polished short story shows evidence of multiple drafts (the polished short story shows it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating finished work, look for signs that lines/structure have been honed and that earlier redundancies or weaknesses have been excised as part of an iterative revision process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization (as subject of workshop analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterization — close readings in workshops (e.g., of Hemingway's opening and endings) focus on how characters are introduced and developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how characters are rendered within the compressed form: whether introductions are economical, whether actions and voice reveal character efficiently, and how characterization supports the story's single effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study of exemplary texts and workshop-based analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use embedded writing workshops (e.g., close reading of specific stories like Oates's 'Labor Day' and 'Where Are You Going, Where Have You Been?') to learn revision and technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn craft by studying model texts and watching revision workshops; apply the methods demonstrated in analyses (openings, characterization, endings) to your own drafts.
